title: Copilot Dashboard: highlights of Copilot adoption from Viva Engage posts
summary: Hold: Microsoft has not documented that every dashboard viewer can see the Engage highlights, that authors are named, or that the view cannot change Engage content. The briefing also omits required app selections in policy creation, the Global Administrator access exception for PIM-enabled tenants, and policy-scope precedence.

claims.quote: Explore how Copilot is making a difference in your organization through Viva Engage posts that users have shared.

claims.claim: The planned posts showcase success stories, excitement about Copilot features and community discussions as qualitative adoption evidence.
claims.quote: The Copilot Dashboard showcases real-world success stories, user-shared excitement about new Copilot features, and vibrant community discussions. These examples offer a qualitative view into how Copilot is driving productivity and engagement across your tenant

claims.claim: The Engage highlights default state and what happens on arrival are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Dashboard" "Viva Engage" highlights licensing price default posts privacy authors; opened copilot-dashboard and manage-settings-copilot-dashboard. The web app's on-by-default statement does not identify this view; the roadmap gives no default.

claims.claim: The web app policy path is Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > feature > Access setting.
claims.quote: Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature.
claims.fix: Include the app selection before the feature: set controls[0].ui.path to 'Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Access setting' and state in its note 'Select the Insights app and the Viva Insights web app feature.' The cited procedure requires both selections.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId VivaInsights, FeatureId 'Viva Insights web app', IsFeatureEnabled $false and Everyone creates a tenant-wide disabling policy.
claims.quote:
Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy
    -FeatureId <String>
    -IsFeatureEnabled <Boolean>
    -ModuleId <String>
    -Name <String>
    [-Confirm]
    [-Everyone]
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchange/add-vivamodulefeaturepolicy to sources for the command syntax. Keep the existing manage-settings citation, which supplies the VivaInsights and Viva Insights web app feature values.

claims.claim: The printed dashboard access path reaches Manage access settings for Microsoft Copilot Dashboard.
claims.quote: Go to the Settings tab and select Microsoft Viva, then Viva Insights. On this page, go to the Set up and management tab. Under Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, select Manage access settings for Microsoft Copilot Dashboard.
claims.fix: Keep the path, which reaches the correct page, and add to controls[1].note: 'To grant access, select Users or Groups, choose the people or groups, then Add. To revoke access, select Users or Groups, choose the entries, then Remove selected users or Remove selected groups.'

claims.claim: No current dedicated automation for the former dashboard access control is documented; the web app policy is the documented scripting alternative.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Insights web app Copilot Dashboard manage access users groups Microsoft Graph API PowerShell; opened manage-settings-copilot-dashboard and Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy. The former dashboard control is no longer available; documented scripting sets web app feature policies.

claims.claim: The auto-enablement policy path is Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > feature > Access setting.
claims.quote: Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy.
claims.fix: Include the app selection before the feature: set controls[2].ui.path to 'Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Access setting' and state in its note 'Select the Insights app and the Copilot Dashboard Auto Enablement feature.'

claims.claim: Dashboard users do not need a paid Viva Insights licence or a Microsoft Copilot licence.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licence tier or licence requirement specific to Engage highlights is not yet published, and the dashboard feature table does not list them.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Dashboard" "Engage" licensing highlights meter billing price; opened copilot-dashboard and its Feature availability based on licenses table; read licensing search excerpts. No result or table entry identifies a tier for Engage highlights.

claims.claim: No meter is documented for Engage highlights at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Dashboard" "Engage" licensing highlights meter billing price; opened copilot-dashboard; read Meters for Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go services and Billing rates and management excerpts. Those meters describe agents, not this dashboard view.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The existing dashboard displays aggregated metrics and hides group metrics below the minimum group size.
claims.quote: Metrics are aggregated at the tenant level or user level, depending on the licenses your tenant has. To protect individual privacy, metrics aren't shown for groups that are smaller than the minimum group size.

claims.claim: The new view puts named employee contributions in front of leaders.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Dashboard" "Viva Engage" read-only posts named authors minimum group size exclusion; opened copilot-dashboard and manage-settings-copilot-dashboard. The roadmap mentions user-shared posts but not whether authors are named.
claims.fix: Replace 'it puts named contributions, not counts, in front of leaders' with 'the roadmap describes user-shared posts rather than only usage counts; Microsoft has not stated whether authors are named'.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a read-only view.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Dashboard" "Viva Engage" read-only posts named authors minimum group size exclusion; opened copilot-dashboard and manage-settings-copilot-dashboard. The record says the dashboard showcases posts, not that the view is read-only.
claims.fix: Replace 'No change: the roadmap describes a read-only view' with 'The roadmap describes showcasing existing Viva Engage posts; it does not describe actions in Engage'.

claims.claim: Nothing is posted or changed in Engage by the highlights feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Dashboard" "Viva Engage" read-only posts named authors minimum group size exclusion; opened copilot-dashboard and manage-settings-copilot-dashboard. No source states that this feature cannot post or change Engage content.
claims.fix: Remove 'Nothing is posted or changed in Engage.' The narrower replacement for the preceding sentence already states what the roadmap describes without asserting an undocumented prohibition.

Read Engage grounding permissions excerpts; these do not place dashboard highlights in that grounding scenario.

claims.where: Scope: Viewers; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Whoever has Copilot Dashboard access can view the Engage highlights, with no documented access change.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Dashboard Viva Engage highlights posts selection authors public communities default licensing meter read only; opened copilot-dashboard, its licence table, and manage-settings-copilot-dashboard. General dashboard access is documented; highlights viewer eligibility is not.
claims.fix: Replace Scope's 'Viewers: whoever has Copilot Dashboard access' with 'Viewers: Microsoft has not documented which dashboard viewers will have access to Engage highlights.' Replace the Security & identity bullet with 'Review existing Copilot Dashboard access using the controls table; feature-specific viewer eligibility is not yet published.'

claims.claim: Some senior leaders have automatic dashboard access in qualifying tenants with at least 2,500 Entra ID users.
claims.quote: Tenants must meet both of the following criteria to qualify: The majority of users in the tenant are part of a single reporting line; The tenant has at least 2,500 users with an Entra ID

claims.claim: Global Administrators automatically have dashboard access.
claims.quote: If you're a Privileged Identity Management (PIM) enabled tenant, global admins might not have access to the Copilot Dashboard. If you want to give global admins access to the Copilot Dashboard, add them explicitly using these steps.
claims.fix: Qualify the Global Administrator statement: 'Global Administrators also have access, but in PIM-enabled tenants they might need to be added explicitly through Manage access settings for Microsoft Copilot Dashboard.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/insights/org-team-insights/copilot-dashboard.

claims.claim: Viva Insights Analysts with global partition access automatically have dashboard access.
claims.quote: The following types of users also have automatic access to the dashboard: Viva Insights Analysts with global partition access

claims.claim: Users with delegate access automatically have dashboard access.
claims.quote: The following types of users also have automatic access to the dashboard: ... Users with delegate access

claims.claim: Enabled managers automatically have dashboard access.
claims.quote: The following types of users also have automatic access to the dashboard: ... Enabled managers.

claims.claim: Changes to the documented web app access policies take effect within 24 hours.
claims.quote: Changes to access policies take effect for the user within 24 hours, unless noted for a specific feature.

claims.claim: The most restrictive policy applies to a user, without distinguishing policy scopes.
claims.quote: Custom policies take precedence over your org-wide settings. For example, if you have organization-wide access turned off, a custom policy could still allow access for specific users or groups.
claims.fix: Replace 'the most restrictive policy applies to a user' with 'user and group policies take precedence over the tenant policy; within the same scope level, the most restrictive enablement policy applies'. This is the scope-first rule at https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/feature-access-management#which-policy-takes-precedence.
